question: Should outbound recovery keep ambiguous entries pending with backoff when no reconciliation-capable adapter is available, instead of moving them to failed?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible: pending preserves future recoverability, while terminal failed gives operators a clearer fail-closed state; tests cannot choose that product and operations tradeoff.

options.title: Accept Recoverable Pending
options.body: Merge after the pacing fix and green exact-head validation if maintainers want no-adapter ambiguous entries to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation ships.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed State
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep current main's terminal failed behavior until the broader delivery ledger is designed.

options.title: Require Operator Surface First
options.body: Ask for a companion doctor, UI, or API surface before changing ambiguous entries to remain pending longer.

recommendation.title: Accept Recoverable Pending
recommendation.body: Merge after the pacing fix and green exact-head validation if maintainers want no-adapter ambiguous entries to remain recoverable until adapter reconciliation ships.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged outbound recovery work and the cross-cutting operator behavior decision point to this owner as the best available routing target.
